By 7950, I mean an AMD graphics card that came out in early 2012.

A graphics card is just a desktop add-in card that people use to play video games. They also happen to be good at "mining" crypto currency, hence the miners buy them in bulk. AMD and Nvidia are the 2 major vendors, but AMD cards are better at mining for a couple of reasons.

But "7950" is just a marketing name. In reality, graphics cards are defined by the chip they use, which has a separate codename. For the AMD 7950/7970 (as well as the 280/280X, and the obscure 7870 XT), that chip was codenamed "Tahiti". They all perform pretty similarly because they use the same de hence savvy miners will see them as roughly equivalent, which is why I used the term.

EDIT: Others you'll probably run into are "Polaris 10" (the RX470/480/570/580), Vega 10/11 (upcoming AMD GPUs), Fiji (the AMD Fury/Nano), GP102 (the Nvidia Titan and 1080 TI,), and GP104 (the 1070/1080).

In 2013 (or hell, was in 2014? I can't remember), Bitcoin prices exploded, leading to an AMD GPU shortage like the one mentioned above.
